speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with a limp and localized pain but no fever. To help me understand your injury, please tell me exactly where the pain is located and what activity you were doing when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (slipped capital femoral epiphysis is also possible, but age and lack of trauma favor Perthes).
